notes.read_only: This map is deliberately READ-ONLY. No compose, reply, send, forward, archive, delete, label, or mark actions exist and none may be added without explicit user approval.
notes.soft_nav: Gmail navigates by location.hash (#inbox, #inbox/<threadid>, #search/<query>) in the TOP document; no preload-iframe trap observed. browser.navigate to a hash URL works for returning to #inbox.

tools.name: gmail.map
tools.description: Return operating guidance for the Gmail read-only survey map. Call this FIRST on Gmail.

static_output.read_only: HARD BOUNDARY: never compose, reply, send, forward, archive, delete, or mark mail as read/unread. Reading is always allowed. SANCTIONED EXCEPTION (approved by the account owner): LABEL management (create/nest/apply labels) and FILTER management (create filters that apply labels) are permitted — these organize mail without altering or transmitting any message. Everything else remains read-only. If a flow ever opens a compose window, press Escape and report.
recommended_sequence: gmail.search (returns the how-to: search runs via browser.navigate to a #search/ URL)
state_read gmail.inbox — rows show sender, subject, snippet, date, unread
gmail.thread.open_by_text — open a conversation by its visible subject/sender text
state_read gmail.thread — full messages with sender email, date, body
static_output.crm_notes: Prospect conversations often MIGRATE here from LinkedIn as they advance. When sweeping for prospects: search each known prospect name AND scan the inbox for personal (non-newsletter) senders. A personal gmail/company address with a conversational subject is a prospect signal even if the name is not yet in the CRM. Match people across platforms by name and company, then keep ONE Trello card per person tracking both channels.
static_output.search_tips: Search by NAVIGATING, not typing: browser.navigate to https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#search/<URL-encoded Gmail query> (e.g. from%3Aalex%20newer_than%3A60d), then read gmail.inbox. The search box does not accept synthetic typing.

tools.name: gmail.search
tools.description: HOW TO SEARCH GMAIL (instruction, not an executor): call the standalone browser.navigate tool yourself with url https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#search/<URL-ENCODED QUERY> (encode spaces as %20, ':' as %3A, '@' as %40). Example: from:alex newer_than:60d → https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#search/from%3Aalex%20newer_than%3A60d . Then read the gmail.inbox projection — result rows use the same markup. Full Gmail query syntax works (from:, subject:, newer_than:60d, OR). Do NOT try to type into the search box.

static_output.how_to_search: browser.navigate to https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#search/<URL-ENCODED QUERY>, then state_read gmail.inbox

tools.name: gmail.thread.open_by_text
tools.description: Open a Gmail conversation from the current row list (inbox or search results) by a distinctive visible substring of its subject or sender. Postcondition proves the thread view (subject header) opened. Read it with the gmail.thread projection. NOTE: opening a thread marks it as read in Gmail — acceptable for the CRM sweep, but be aware.

row_text.description: Distinctive substring of the row's visible subject or sender, e.g. 'Alex Doe' or a subject fragment.

x_state_machine.requires_state: row list visible (inbox or search results)

workflow.output: {% {'opened_row': input.row_text, 'thread_open': $exists(steps.threadOpen.output), 'note': 'Read the gmail.thread projection for the messages. Return to the list with browser.navigate to .../#inbox or by re-running gmail.search.'} %}

state_projections.name: gmail.inbox
state_projections.description: The visible Gmail row list (inbox OR search results — same markup): per row sender name/email, subject, snippet, date, unread flag. The agent's eyes on the mailbox. Rows are the currently rendered page (~50-100); older mail needs gmail.search with newer_than/older_than.

state_projections.name: gmail.thread
state_projections.description: The currently open Gmail conversation: subject plus each message's sender name/email, date, and body text (bodies truncated to 1500 chars). Use after gmail.thread.open_by_text.
